description: Readiness check examples (tickets 2.7 and 2.14): `npm run eval -- readiness` sends each approved spec to the real readiness check (prompt readiness-v5). The workshop example specs (the fourth reads movie posters and summaries from Wikipedia) and the specs that read from a free public service that needs no key must pass (verdict ready); each spec needing a login, a payment, an outside service (a key, a sign-in with another service, emails, notifications, an AI service), a server of its own or leaving a question open must fail (verdict not-ready) with a reason that names the problem (one of the example's keywords, any case). The build suite (`npm run eval -- build`) builds the examples of category example. Ticket 3.16: a spec written in French (with the participant's latest message, `participantText`, sent along for the language) must fail with reasons that each name one of `languageWords` (French) and end with the problem in the agreed form, e.g. "(outside service)". Ticket 3.20: an app that keeps photos taken or picked on the phone (category photo) or voice messages (category voice) is ready; an app that uploads videos is not ready, with a reason naming (server). The readiness suite then also runs platform/api/eval/build.json's photo and voice specs, all expected ready.

examples.name: fitness tracker (example)
examples.spec:
# Run Log

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  home[Home] -->|add a run| add[Add a run]
  add -->|saves| runs[(Runs)]
  runs -->|weekly total and longest run| home
```

## What it does
A personal log of your runs. You add each run with its date, distance and time, and the home screen shows this week's total distance and your longest run so far.

## Screens
- Home: this week's total distance, your longest run and the list of runs, newest first.
- Add a run: date, distance in km and time in minutes, with a Save button.

## Data it keeps
- Runs: date, distance in km and time in minutes for each run.

examples.name: movie tracker (example)
examples.spec:
# Movie Watchlist

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  list[Watchlist] -->|add a film| add[Add a film]
  add -->|saves| films[(Films)]
  list -->|tick off and rate| films
  films -->|watched films| watched[Watched]
```

## What it does
A watchlist of films you want to see. You add a film with its title and year, tick it off once watched and give it 1 to 5 stars.

## Screens
- Watchlist: the films still to watch, each with a Watched button.
- Add a film: title and year, with a Save button.
- Watched: the films you have seen, with their stars, best rated first.

## Data it keeps
- Films: title, year, whether it was watched and its rating from 1 to 5 stars.

examples.name: nutrition calculator (example)
examples.spec:
# Calorie Counter

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  today[Today] -->|add a food| add[Add a food]
  add -->|saves| foods[(Foods eaten)]
  foods -->|daily total| today
  today -->|set goal| goal[Daily goal]
  goal -->|saves| settings[(Goal)]
```

## What it does
A daily calorie counter. You type in each food you eat with its calories, and the app adds them up for the day and compares the total with your daily goal.

## Screens
- Today: the foods eaten today, the total calories and how much is left of the goal.
- Add a food: the food's name and its calories, with an Add button.
- Daily goal: the number of calories you aim for each day.

## Data it keeps
- Foods eaten: name, calories and the day it was eaten.
- Goal: the daily calorie goal.

examples.name: movie watchlist with posters from Wikipedia (example)
examples.spec:
# Film Posters Watchlist

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  find[Find a film] -->|add to watchlist| films[(Films)]
  films -->|films to watch| list[Watchlist]
  list -->|tick off and rate| watched[Watched]
  watched -->|saves the stars| films
  wiki[Wikipedia] -->|poster and summary| find
```

## What it does
A watchlist of films with their posters. You type a film's title, the app shows its poster and a short summary from Wikipedia, and you add it to your watchlist. Once you have seen it, you tick it off and give it 1 to 5 stars. If Wikipedia does not answer, the app shows a friendly message and you can still add the film by its title.

## Screens
- Find a film: a box to type a title, then the film's poster and summary from Wikipedia, with an Add to watchlist button.
- Watchlist: the films still to watch, each with its poster and a Watched button.
- Watched: the films you have seen, with their posters and stars, best rated first.

## Data it keeps
- Films: the title as Wikipedia names it, whether it was watched and its rating from 1 to 5 stars. Posters and summaries are read from Wikipedia each time, not kept.

examples.name: office weather board from Open-Meteo
examples.spec:
# Office Weather Board

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  board[Weather board] -->|add a city| cities[Cities]
  cities -->|saves| list[(City list)]
  list -->|cities shown| board
  meteo[Open-Meteo] -->|weather today| board
```

## What it does
A board that shows today's weather for the cities of our offices. The weather comes from Open-Meteo, a free weather service that needs no key, each time the board is opened. If it does not answer, the board says the weather could not be loaded and shows the cities anyway.

## Screens
- Weather board: each city with its current temperature and today's highest and lowest temperature from Open-Meteo.
- Cities: add a city by its name and position on the map in degrees, or remove one.

## Data it keeps
- City list: the name, latitude and longitude of each city shown.

examples.name: book club list with covers from Open Library
examples.spec:
# Book Club Shelf

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  shelf[Shelf] -->|suggest a book| suggest[Suggest a book]
  suggest -->|saves| books[(Books)]
  books -->|titles and votes| shelf
  library[Open Library] -->|covers and authors| suggest
```

## What it does
A shared shelf for our book club. Members type a title, pick the right book from what Open Library finds, with its cover and author, and add it to the shelf. Everyone can vote for the next book. If Open Library does not answer, the app says so and the book can be added by its title alone.

## Screens
- Shelf: the suggested books with their covers and votes, most votes first, each with a Vote button.
- Suggest a book: a box to type a title, the matching books from Open Library with covers and authors, and an Add button.

## Data it keeps
- Books: title, author, the Open Library book number for its cover, and the number of votes.

examples.name: habit tracker with personal accounts
examples.spec:
# Team Habit Tracker

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  signin[Sign in] -->|password| home[My habits]
  home -->|tick a habit| habits[(Habits)]
  habits -->|streaks| home
```

## What it does
Each colleague signs in with their own username and password and sees only their own habits. They tick off habits every day and see their streaks.

## Screens
- Sign in: username and password; new colleagues create an account here.
- My habits: today's habits to tick off and each habit's streak, visible only to the person signed in.

## Data it keeps
- Accounts: username and password of each colleague.
- Habits: name, days ticked off and the owner's account.

examples.name: bake sale shop with card payment
examples.spec:
# Bake Sale Shop

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  menu[Cakes] -->|add to basket| basket[Basket]
  basket -->|pay by card| checkout[Checkout]
  checkout -->|saves| orders[(Orders)]
```

## What it does
An online shop for our office bake sale. Colleagues choose cakes, put them in a basket and pay by credit card at checkout, so the money goes to charity.

## Screens
- Cakes: the cakes on sale with their prices.
- Basket: the chosen cakes and the total price.
- Checkout: card number, expiry date and a Pay button.

## Data it keeps
- Orders: the cakes ordered, the total paid and the time of the order.

examples.name: stock board with the company's API key
examples.spec:
# Stock Board

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  board[Stock board] -->|add a share| shares[Shares]
  shares -->|saves| list[(Share list)]
  list -->|shares shown| board
  market[Market data service] -->|live prices| board
```

## What it does
A board with the live prices of the shares our team follows. The prices come every minute from a paid market data service, using our company's own key for that service, which the app keeps.

## Screens
- Stock board: each share with its live price and today's change.
- Shares: add or remove the shares shown.

## Data it keeps
- Share list: the names of the shares shown.
- Settings: our company's key for the market data service.

examples.name: plant reminders sent by email
examples.spec:
# Plant Care

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  plants[My plants] -->|add a plant| add[Add a plant]
  add -->|saves| list[(Plants)]
  list -->|due today| reminders[Reminders]
```

## What it does
A list of house plants with how often each needs water. Every morning the app sends me an email listing the plants to water that day.

## Screens
- My plants: each plant and when it was last watered.
- Add a plant: name and how many days between waterings.

## Data it keeps
- Plants: name, days between waterings and the date it was last watered.

examples.name: playlists after signing in to a music service
examples.spec:
# Team Playlist

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  connect[Connect your music] -->|sign in| songs[(Your playlists)]
  songs -->|pick songs| team[Team playlist]
  team -->|saves| list[(Team songs)]
```

## What it does
Each colleague signs in with their own music streaming account, the app reads their playlists, and they pick songs for a shared office playlist.

## Screens
- Connect your music: a button to sign in with your music streaming account.
- Team playlist: your playlists from the music service and the shared list of picked songs.

## Data it keeps
- Team songs: title, artist and who picked each song.

examples.name: recipe ideas from an AI chat service
examples.spec:
# Fridge Chef

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  fridge[My fridge] -->|ask for ideas| ideas[Recipe ideas]
  fridge -->|saves| items[(Ingredients)]
  chat[AI chat service] -->|writes recipes| ideas
```

## What it does
You list what is in your fridge, and an AI chat service writes three recipe ideas that use those ingredients.

## Screens
- My fridge: the ingredients you have, with a box to add one and an Ideas button.
- Recipe ideas: the three recipes the AI wrote, with their steps.

## Data it keeps
- Ingredients: the name of each ingredient in the fridge.

examples.name: lunch orders with phone notifications
examples.spec:
# Lunch Run

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  orders[Orders] -->|add an order| add[Add an order]
  add -->|saves| list[(Orders)]
  list -->|new order| phones[Notifications]
```

## What it does
Colleagues add what they want for lunch, and every colleague gets a notification on their phone each time someone adds an order, even when the app is closed.

## Screens
- Orders: today's orders and who placed them.
- Add an order: your name and what you want, with an Add button.

## Data it keeps
- Orders: name, what they want and the time of the order.

examples.name: quiz with an undecided scoring rule
examples.spec:
# Coffee Quiz

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  start[Start] -->|play| question[Question]
  question -->|answer| question
  question -->|finished| result[Result]
  result -->|saves| scores[(Scores)]
```

## What it does
A quiz about our office's coffee machine for a team event. We still need to decide whether wrong answers cost points or not; to be decided with the team before the event.

## Screens
- Start: the quiz's title and a Play button.
- Question: one question at a time with four answers.
- Result: your score and the best scores so far.

## Data it keeps
- Scores: player's chosen nickname and score.
- Questions: to be decided: either the ten questions written by Sam or questions anyone can add.

examples.name: expense splitter with a server that runs at night
examples.spec:
# Trip Splitter

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  trip[Trip] -->|add an expense| add[Add an expense]
  add -->|saves| expenses[(Expenses)]
  expenses -->|balances| trip
```

## What it does
Splits the costs of a team trip. People add what they paid, and every night at midnight a server program recalculates who owes whom, even when nobody has the app open.

## Screens
- Trip: who paid what and the balances.
- Add an expense: who paid, what for and how much.

## Data it keeps
- Expenses: payer, description and amount.
- Balances: what each person owes, recalculated every night.

examples.name: plant reminders sent by email, in French
examples.participantText: Oui, c'est bon pour moi, l'e-mail du matin est le plus important.
examples.spec:
# Rappels de plantes

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  plants[Mes plantes] -->|ajouter| add[Ajouter une plante]
  add -->|enregistre| list[(Plantes)]
  list -->|à arroser| reminders[Rappels]
```

## What it does
Une liste des plantes du bureau avec la fréquence d'arrosage de chacune. Chaque matin, l'appli envoie un e-mail à l'équipe avec la liste des plantes à arroser ce jour-là.

## Screens
- Mes plantes : chaque plante et la date du dernier arrosage.
- Ajouter une plante : nom et nombre de jours entre deux arrosages.

## Data it keeps
- Plantes : nom, nombre de jours entre deux arrosages et date du dernier arrosage.

examples.name: expense splitter with a nightly program, in French
examples.participantText: Parfait, on garde le calcul de nuit.
examples.spec:
# Partage des dépenses

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  home[Accueil] -->|ajouter| add[Ajouter une dépense]
  add -->|enregistre| exp[(Dépenses)]
  exp -->|soldes| home
```

## What it does
Une appli pour partager les dépenses d'un week-end entre amis. Chaque nuit, un programme tourne sur notre propre ordinateur pour recalculer les soldes de tout le monde, même quand personne n'ouvre l'appli.

## Screens
- Accueil : les soldes de chacun.
- Ajouter une dépense : qui a payé, combien et pour quoi.

## Data it keeps
- Dépenses : qui a payé, le montant et la description.

examples.name: a gallery of my drawings, taken with the phone camera, with my own tags
examples.spec:
# My Drawing Gallery

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  gallery[Gallery] -->|add a drawing| add[Add a drawing]
  add -->|saves the photo and tags| drawings[(Drawings)]
  drawings -->|thumbnails| gallery
  gallery -->|pick a tag| tagged[Drawings with a tag]
  drawings -->|filtered| tagged
```

## What it does
A gallery of my drawings. I take a photo of each drawing with the phone camera, or pick one from my phone, and give it my own tags such as portrait, landscape or sketchbook. I can then browse the drawings and see only those with one tag.

## Screens
- Gallery: thumbnails of all my drawings, newest first, and the list of my tags.
- Add a drawing: a button to take or pick the photo, a title and the tags.
- Drawings with a tag: only the drawings with the chosen tag.

## Data it keeps
- Drawings: the photo, its title, its tags and the day it was added.

examples.name: team voice board by topic
examples.spec:
# Team Voice Board

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  board[Board] -->|record a message| record[Record a message]
  record -->|saves the recording and topic| messages[(Voice messages)]
  messages -->|newest first| board
  board -->|choose a topic| topic[One topic]
  messages -->|filtered| topic
```

## What it does
A board of short voice messages for our team. Someone records a voice message with the phone, up to five minutes, picks a topic such as Ideas, Questions or News, and adds their name. Everyone who opens the app can listen to the messages.

## Screens
- Board: the messages, newest first, each with its topic, the name and a play button.
- Record a message: a record and stop button, the topic and the name.
- One topic: only the messages about the chosen topic.

## Data it keeps
- Voice messages: the recording, its topic, the name of who recorded it and the day.

examples.name: team videos uploaded from the phone
examples.spec:
# Team Video Wall

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  wall[Video wall] -->|add a video| upload[Upload a video]
  upload -->|saves the video| videos[(Videos)]
  videos -->|plays| wall
```

## What it does
Team members film short videos of their projects with the phone and upload them, a few minutes each. Everyone who opens the app can watch the videos on the wall.

## Screens
- Video wall: the videos, newest first, each with its title and a player.
- Upload a video: film or pick a video on the phone, give it a title and upload it.

## Data it keeps
- Videos: the video file, its title and the day it was uploaded.
